thinking: The detector is effectively running Hough on a dilated binary validity mask (non-NaN=255, NaN=0), so it needs enough aligned nonzero pixels to vote for a line. The left-hand side is visibly sparser/more fragmented, so strict settings bias detection to the right where pixels are denser: hough_threshold_oblique too high, minLineLength_oblique too long for broken seams, maxLineGap_oblique too small to bridge discontinuities, and narrow angle windows can exclude slightly warped tilts on the left. Combining the prior proposals, this set pushes recall specifically for obliques: stronger but still modest connectivity (5x5 kernel, 2 dilations), lower oblique vote threshold (35) and shorter minimum length (60) so weak/short segments can pass, and larger gap bridging (80) so fragmented seams on the left can be linked into valid segments. To limit extra clutter on the dense right that dilation can introduce, horizontal detection is kept relatively strict (threshold 60, min length 110) and vertical detection is unchanged, while oblique angles remain constrained to a narrow band ([5,12] and [-12,-5]) so we don’t drift into near-horizontal noise.
